'''Klatooinians''' were a [[Humanoid/Legends|humanoid]] [[Species/Legends|species]] from the [[Planet/Legends|planet]] [[Klatooine/Legends|Klatooine]], located in the [[Si'Klaata Cluster/Legends|Si'Klaata Cluster]]. For most of their history, they were closely associated with the [[Hutt/Legends|Hutts]], as criminal henchmen, soldiers, and [[Slavery/Legends|slaves]]. By the time of the [[Galactic Civil War/Legends|Galactic Civil War]], however, some Klatooinians began to break away from their servitude.

==History==
[[File:Klatooinian_NEGAS.jpg|thumb|left|190px|A Klatooinian]]
{{Quote|They've been in service to the Hutts for over twenty-five thousand years.|Luke Skywalker|<ref name="Fate of the Jedi: Allies">''[[Fate of the Jedi: Allies]]''</ref>}}
When the Hutts were waging a [[Xim Wars|war]] against [[Xim/Legends|Xim the Despot]] circa [[25,100 BBY]], they looked for help on some of the planets in the [[Si'Klaata Cluster/Legends|Si'Klaata Cluster]]. Hutt envoys asked Klatooinians to become part of their army. Klatooinians thought of it as a sacred war, and [[Barada M'Beg]] signed a treaty promising that Klatooinians would be slaves of the Hutts forever.

After the defeat of Xim at the [[Third Battle of Vontor]], Klatooinians continued to serve the Hutts under the terms of the [[Treaty of Vontor]]. Many of their children were named Barada or M'Beg to honor Barada M'Beg.<ref name="gg12">''[[Galaxy Guide 12: Aliens — Enemies and Allies]]''</ref> Other common Klatooinian names included Bekure, Drekk, Jarakar, Massa, Rokar, and Sovara.<ref name="Ultimate Alien Anthology" />

The Klatooinians revered the Hutts, whose natural lifespan spanned several centuries, as near-gods&mdash;possibly even the [[Ancients]] of Klatooinian myth. In fact, the [[Fountain of Ancients]] was renamed the Fountain of Hutt Ancients. Under Hutt rule, the Klatooinian elders were allowed to rule Klatooine, but all off-world concerns, such as the infamous [[Klatooinian Trade Guild/Legends|Klatooinian Trade Guild]], were wholly under Hutt control. In [[44 ABY]], damage to the Fountain of Ancients by Sith operatives served as a pretense for the Klatoonians to declare the Treaty of Vontor breached by the Hutt, thus voiding their enslavement. Widespread slave revolts marked the Klatoonian uprising, which was part of a larger anti-slavery movement in [[The galaxy/Legends|the Galaxy]] at the time.

==Society and culture==
{{Quote|I wouldn't dismiss them quite so quickly. They may not be attractive to your eyes, Vestara, but their culture predates even the Old Republic. You're looking at one of the oldest species in the galaxy.|Luke Skywalker to Vestara Khai|<ref name="Fate of the Jedi: Allies" />}}
Klatooinian civilization was notable for its strong belief in tradition and the wisdom of elders. The center of their culture was the Fountain of Ancients, a slowly evolving natural glass sculpture on Klatooine's [[Derelkoos Desert]]. Long before the formation of the [[Galactic Republic/Legends|Galactic Republic]], primitive Klatooinians discovered the Fountain, and revered it as a symbol of patience, tenacity, and the idea of strength coming from age.

Their society was ruled by a [[Council of Elders (Klatooinian)|Council of Elders]], who granted young Klatooinians few rights. Klatooinians were taught the myths and traditions of their people from a young age, in a process which tended to suppress individuality. At the age of ten, they would be sold into servitude, with the most rebellious youths sent into the harshest conditions.

==Klatooinians in the galaxy==
[[File:Klatoonian_roustabout.jpg|thumb|left|200px|A Klatooinian roustabout]]
Other Klatooinians served non-Hutt masters. The [[Dark side adept/Legends|Dark Side Adept]] [[Professor/Legends|Profex]] [[Rynalla]] once traveled to the planet [[Leritor/Legends|Leritor]] with an entourage of two dozen Klatooinians, who served her as soldiers and slavers by kidnapping locals and forcing them to search for a secret [[Sith artifact/Legends|Sith treasure]].<ref name="g10">{{GamerCite|10|Standoff on Leritor}}</ref> During the [[Clone Wars/Legends|Clone Wars]] there was a [[Bounty hunter/Legends|bounty hunter]] named [[Castas/Legends|Castas]] who worked alongside [[Aurra Sing/Legends|Aurra Sing]], [[Bossk/Legends|Bossk]], and [[Boba Fett/Legends|Boba Fett]].<ref name="R2 Come Home">{{TCW|R2 Come Home}}</ref>

Despite being vassals of the Hutts, some Klatooinians served the Galactic Republic as part of the [[Jedi Order/Legends|Jedi Order]]. The [[Jedi/Legends|Jedi]] [[Sta-Den Eekin/Legends|Sta-Den Eekin]] and [[Tarados Gon/Legends|Tarados Gon]] were killed during the [[First Battle of Geonosis/Legends|First Battle of Geonosis]].<ref name="Jedi Casualties">{{Blog|holocron|10|Jedi Casualties: Battle of Geonosis}}</ref>

During the Galactic Civil War, many young Klatooinians were inspired by the [[Alliance to Restore the Republic/Legends|Rebel Alliance's]] message of freedom, and such Rebel victories as the [[Battle of Yavin/Legends|Battle of Yavin]]. Many young Klatooinians turned their backs on tradition and rebelled against their former masters, sometimes joining up with [[Smuggler/Legends|smugglers]], [[Pirate/Legends|pirates]], or rival criminal organizations. Some remained on their [[Homeworld/Legends|homeworld]], hiding in the wilderness. A few, such as the technologist [[Rolanda Gron]], managed to join the Rebellion themselves. During the [[Yuuzhan Vong War]], a Klatooinian was a [[Galactic Federation of Free Alliances|Galactic Alliance]] spy in the [[Peace Brigade]].

Most Klatooinians, however, remained servants of the Hutts, working for the Klatooinian Trade Guild or various Hutt [[Kajidic/Legends|kajidics]]. Indeed, their servitude continued well into the time of the [[New Republic/Legends|New Republic]]. [[Jabba Desilijic Tiure/Legends|Jabba the Hutt]] had several Klatooinians in his employ, including [[Barada/Legends|Barada]], the chief mechanic on the [[Khetanna/Legends|''Khetanna'']], [[Kithaba/Legends|Kithaba]], a famous [[assassin]], and [[Umpass-stay/Legends|Umpass-stay]], his bodyguard, spy, and drummer. [[File:CastasFull-R2CH.png|thumb|right|150px|[[Castas/Legends|Castas]], a Klatooinian bounty hunter]]

==Behind the scenes==
In the expanded universe, including ''[[Heir to the Empire]]'' and [[Star Wars: Tales of the Jedi (miniseries)|''Star Wars: Tales of the Jedi'']] the Klatooinians were originally referred to as "[[Barada/Legends|Baradas]]."

The PC game [[Star Wars: Rebellion (video game)|''Star Wars: Rebellion'']] describes the Klatooinian species as having two tentacles coming from their heads. This seems to be a mistaken reference to the [[Twi'lek/Legends|Twi'lek]] species.

There seems to be some discrepancy regarding Klatooinian hands. In the Prequel Trilogy, the Klatooinians have elongated, sharp claws that resemble blades, though in the artwork for ''[[The New Essential Guide to Alien Species]]'' and in the original trilogy the Klatooinians have human-like hands. Whether there are two subspecies of Klatooinian or not is unknown.
